en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its nearly perfect cone shape and is the most active volcano in the Philippines.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through Cagayan Valley before emptying into the Luzon Strait.
Lake Lanao in Mindanao is the largest lake in the Philippines by surface area and serves as a major source of hydroelectric power.
The Philippine eagle, also called the monkey-eating eagle, is the national bird of the Philippines and is currently classified as critically endangered.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of exactly 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features an eight-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the West Philippine Sea.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site famous for its pristine coral reefs and marine biodiversity.
The island province of Batanes is the northernmost province in the Philippines and is famous for its traditional stone houses with thick limestone walls.
The Cordillera Administrative Region contains the Banaue Rice Terraces, which are ancient agricultural landscapes carved into the mountains by the indigenous Ifugao people.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, is one of the smallest primates in the world and has enormous eyes adapted for nocturnal hunting.
Boracay Island in Aklan province is a globally recognized tourist destination famous for its White Beach, which consists of fine crushed coral sand.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season, resembling chocolate kisses.
